REC_0001,BIM-Assisted UAV Topological Localization and Navigation Method for GPS-Denied Indoor Environments,"Hao Pan, Haowei Ye, Wei Zheng, Lv Zhou",2026,2026 6th International Conference on Control and Intelligent Robotics (ICCIR),10.1109/ICCIR70228.2026.11633308,"China (Nanchang Hangkong University, Jiangxi)","""However, reliable indoor UAV operation fundamentally depends on robust localization and navigation capabilities. Unlike outdoor environments, indoor scenarios typically suffer from unavailable or severely degraded Global Positioning System (GPS) signals"" [p.1].","""Existing indoor localization approaches mainly focus on recovering continuous metric coordinates and performing navigation on geometric maps[5]. Chen et al. [6] transformed BIM semantic and geometric information into a graph structure for UAV navigation, improving the interpretability of indoor path planning. However, the approach primarily focused on navigation planning and assumed that the UAV location was already known, failing to address localization ambiguity caused by repetitive corridors and visually similar rooms in GPS-denied indoor environments."" [p.1].","""The proposed framework transforms BIM into a lightweight semantic-topological graph and converts UAV image observations into candidate BIM node sets using spatial semantic recognition and OCR-based textual cues. A topology-aware recursive localization mechanism is then introduced, integrating BIM adjacency constraints and historical states to continuously infer the most probable topological node. Furthermore, semantic-cost A* path planning is employed to verify whether the estimated topological locations can effectively support indoor UAV navigation tasks."" [p.3]","""The proposed framework was implemented in Python using PyTorch for image semantic classification and NetworkX for BIM topology construction and path planning. UAV perception input was simulated using monocular image sequences collected in a real university teaching-building environment containing repetitive corridors, room entrances, and staircase regions.""
